_comment: Hits from scripts/i18n-diacritics.mjs that a human read and judged correct as written.
The detector has no dictionary: it infers from frequency inside one locale file, so a word
that merely folds onto a more common accented word looks identical to a stripped one.
Roughly four in five hits are this. Suppressing them here is what keeps the gate readable,
and a readable gate is the whole point, because it exists to catch the NEXT one.
An entry is keyed by locale, key AND value, so rewording a string retires its acceptance:
the judgement was about that sentence, not about that key forever.
Never bulk-accept. Every line here was read against the language, not against the tool.

accepted.cy\u001fsettings.githubOauthDesc\u001fDe: Correct as written. The flagged word is 'Client' inside 'Client ID', which is the literal name of the field in GitHub's OAuth app settings and must stay in English so the user can match it on screen. Welsh 'client' in the ordinary sense is indeed spelled clïent, which is why it folds onto the six other occurrences in this file, but that is a different word from this identifier.
accepted.lv\u001fsyncPanel.schedulerTimeWindow\u0: Correct as written. 'laika' is the genitive of 'laiks', which is the case Latvian needs for 'window OF time'. The form the detector prefers, 'laika' with a macron, is the locative and means 'in time' or 'during', a different sentence. The accented twin is more frequent in this file simply because it is the commoner form in prose, not because it is right here.
